arguments.value: This agreement appoints the agency to solicit and service MICOA health care and professional liability insurance business in Nevada, but the agency cannot bind MICOA without permission. The agency must follow MICOA underwriting rules, report claims promptly, avoid advertising without approval, and generally work exclusively for MICOA on the listed professional liability products unless MICOA declines a risk. MICOA pays commissions on business it bills directly, and the agency’s name must appear on policy documents and notices. If the agreement ends, MICOA must buy the agency’s interest in expirations for the business produced under the agreement, and the agency is then restricted from selling to those MICOA insureds for two years. The agency must keep errors-and-omissions and fidelity/electronic crime insurance in force. Either party can terminate on notice, and MICOA can terminate immediately for serious misconduct, license issues, or delinquent payments. The parties must indemnify each other for their own acts or omissions, disputes go to binding arbitration, the agreement is governed by Nevada law, and the agency is an independent contractor. A related memorandum says MICOA helped fund Nevada startup costs for the agency’s Nevada operation, with repayment through reduced commissions over time, and set forth shared expenses and a 12% commission rate for Nevada physicians professional liability business.
